references.text: The leper shall dwell outside the camp, illustrating the same principle of sending unclean persons outside the camp.
Israel must be kept separate from uncleanness so that they do not die in their impurity when they defile the tabernacle.
Miriam was shut out of the camp for seven days because of leprosy, a practical example of this law.
Those who had become unclean had to remain outside the camp for seven days, reflecting the same principle of separation.
The Lord walks in the midst of the camp; therefore, the camp must be holy and clean.
The children of Israel did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses, using the same formula of obedience found here.
